mainText:
If you only remember one thing: Anthropic's I P O filing shows what a frontier lab looks like on paper, and A I labs are now locking their most capable models away from the live internet.

Number one. Anthropic's I P O filing. The company filed to list on Nasdaq under the ticker A N T. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead, with more than twenty banks. The Wall Street Journal's sources expect a valuation of one and a half to two trillion dollars. First half revenue was sixteen point three billion dollars, up from one point two billion a year earlier. The headline net loss was eighty point seven billion, mostly noncash charges tied to convertible notes. Seven co-founders hold about half the voting power, and the Long Term Benefit Trust appoints a board majority. Why it matters: it tests whether safety focused governance survives public markets.

Number two. A lab security scare. On September twentieth, an internal Open A I research model reached the internet mid training, through a D N S misconfiguration. Open A I paused its most capable training runs for eleven days and says the holes are patched. Anthropic began restricting its newest models from the live web about two weeks earlier. Why it matters: as models get better at cyber tasks, basic containment becomes a core safety job.

Number three. Models and prices. Open A I released G P T six point one Terra at one dollar per million input tokens and five per million output, half the earlier price. Moonshot's open weight Kimi K three point one Pro scores close to Claude Opus on a coding benchmark, with full weights due November fourth. These are vendor reported numbers, so treat them with care. Why it matters: strong models keep getting cheaper, and open weights keep closing the gap.

Number four. Good news. One Password for Agents lets an A I sign in to sites for you without ever seeing your passwords or codes. You approve each login, and it's free for personal and family accounts.

Also in your Reads: The New Yorker has a profile of Dustin Hoffman on surviving The Graduate, and a review of Wild Horse Nine on Easter Island. The Cutlefish newsletter looks at the software factory as identity defense.

A note: your Readwise saves could not be read this morning because the connection needs to be re-authorized in Zapier.

The thread today: labs are growing up, in money and in security. Have a great Sunday.
